subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw notify — admin-scoped push to connected UI sessions

question: Should OpenClaw core expose a shell-facing admin notification broadcast to connected Control UI sessions, and what auth scope, payload, targeting, delivery, and abuse-control contract should it use?
rationale: The current code lacks the requested surface, but adding it creates a new core Gateway/UI API and security boundary that automation should not choose by implication.

options.title: Define a narrow core notify contract
options.body: Add an explicit admin-scoped CLI/Gateway/Control UI notification path with sanitized payloads, targeting semantics, rate/abuse controls, docs, and focused tests.

options.title: Fold into the broader WebUI notification tracker
options.body: Make #20237 explicitly own the shell/admin Gateway API before closing or merging this issue into the broader toast architecture work.

options.title: Keep outside core for now
options.body: Defer the feature to plugins/hooks or future plugin API work until maintainers decide core should own connected-UI notifications.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow core notify contract
recommendation.body: Add an explicit admin-scoped CLI/Gateway/Control UI notification path with sanitized payloads, targeting semantics, rate/abuse controls, docs, and focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger is the strongest available current-main owner signal for the system CLI and Gateway broadcast/security boundary that would need the API decision.
